extracted.intended_audience: early modern natural philosophers, physicians, surgeons, and antiquarians (readers/members of the Royal Society)
extracted.subtask_description: Observational reports and short communications describing natural objects, medical cases, antiquities, and meteorological/biological observations, with embedded methods for documenting, identifying, and treating phenomena. The page mixes specimen description, dissection/surgical technique, and historical/philological documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing transparent pebbles (brontiae) as mineral vs organic
rubrics_metrics.description: These pebbles ... are of a very different nature and texture from all other ombriae I ever yet saw, and have no vestigia of any spinas in any part of them, they may be concluded to be stones of their own kind; and though they are in shape like some of the ombriae, yet they will not, I think, come within the suspicion of having been animal substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess texture and internal structure: very hard and solid; do not consist of laminae or flakes; break with difficulty and naturally smooth throughout. Compare to known ombriae species and references (Aldrovandus, Scilla, Dr. Plot). Absence of spines/vestigia suggests non-animal origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use microscopy to distinguish natural from artificial polish
rubrics_metrics.description: Their natural polish is not to be counterfeited, but very easy to be distinguished by a microscope from the artificial polish of glass and crystals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine surface under a microscope to differentiate natural polish (characteristic microtexture) from machine/heat-polished glass or crystal surfaces. Do not rely solely on macroscopic shine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and documentation for epigraphic recording (Persepolis characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper ... containing the exact Draughts of several unknown Characters, taken from the Ruins at Persepolis. ... Some of the characters seem to be very ancient Greek, some have a resemblance to Hebrew, mixed with other forms; others again resemble the Arabic or Persian character ... one has some affinity with the old Syriac and Arabic; and one is the nail character, or pyramid shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create exact draughts/engravings of inscriptions in situ and preserve papers/plates; compare shapes to known alphabets (Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Syriac) to infer affinities; note which characters are illegible to local experts and report those uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferring hummingbird diet from morphology and dissection
rubrics_metrics.description: It is believed the humming bird feeds on some juice he sucks from flowers. Whether may not this bird rather feed on small insects ... The bird should be opened, and so it will appear either that he has entrails fitted only for liquids, or the same sort of stomachs and guts as other birds, containing the same sort of solid food.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bill and tongue morphology (e.g., tongue a double tube) to hypothesize feeding mode; confirm by dissection to examine stomach structure and contents (liquid-only apparatus vs presence of solid-food-adapted guts). Consider comparing to insect-sucking organisms (bees) that possess a siphon/hollow probe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paschal's time-division method for correlating births/deaths/disease motions
rubrics_metrics.description: I divided the natural day into four senaries of hours; the first consisted of 3 hours before the moon's southing, and 3 after; the second of the 6 hours following, and so the third and fourth contained the two remaining quarters of the natural day. I observed the times of the births and deaths in human creatures, and also in other animals ... I found none that were born or died a natural death in the first and third senaries ... every one either in the second or fourth senaries. ... motion, vigour, action, strength, &c. appear most, and do best, in the tiding senaries, and that rest, relaxation, decay, dissolution, belong to the ebbing senaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To test temporal/astronomical hypotheses: define explicit time-windows tied to lunar position (senaries), systematically record events (births, deaths, disease fits) and analyze their distribution across windows; control for non-naturals (sex res non naturales), weather, and other confounders; report any consistent pattern and its limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-incisional extraction technique for bladder stones in women (operative steps and indications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The surgeon passed his catheter into the neck of the bladder, that it might empty itself of all urine, before he inserted his dilating instrument, or his speculum viscae ... afterwards by help of a directory and forceps, gently thrust into the bladder, he brought away the stone without any manner of incision ... The child was placed in a convenient posture ... with her arms tied down to her legs ... extracted in about 3 or 4 minutes ... put the patient to so little manner of pain ... now perfectly well and at ease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications: stone not immoderately large and amenable to dilation. Procedure: position patient (seated across a table in lap), catheterize to empty bladder, dilate urethra carefully with speculum/dilator, use director and forceps to grasp and remove stone; restrain patient appropriately to prevent motion. Advantages: avoids section/incision; applicable to children and adults when anatomy permits. Monitor for and counsel about possible sphincter stretch/incontinence after passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognizing bladder stones adhered to bladder membrane
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stones ... must of necessity remain fixed in the bladder; being closely joined and united to the very substance of its membrane ... about the larger end, there still closely adheres several thin films and carneous filaments, which manifestly show it was formerly united by this part to the membranous substance of the bladder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect extracted stones for adhering thin films or carneous filaments as evidence of prior union to bladder membrane. Such adherence influences the expectation of spontaneous passage and may guide the choice between extraction techniques versus incision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification characters and seasonality of truffles (Tubera terrae)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tubera terrae ... are all included in a studded bark or coat, the tubercules resembling the capsules or seed-vessels of some mallows and alceas; the inward substance is of the consistence of the fleshy part in a young chesnut, of a paste colour, of a rank odour, and unsavoury, streaked with many white veins or threads; the whole is of a globose figure, though unequal and chinky.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify truffles by external studded bark and internal paste-like flesh with white veins and strong scent. Note phenology: most tender in spring; abundant after showers and in autumn. Ecological cues: wet conditions swell them; animals (swine) are attracted to scent. Use morphological and seasonal criteria rather than assumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary method for historical-philosophical inquiry (Burnet example)
rubrics_metrics.description: He divides the whole discourse into two books. In the first he endeavours to discover what were the most ancient doctrines of all nations concerning the beginnings of things ... in the second he endeavours to collect all such passages among them, as seemed most consonant to, and confirming of the doctrines delivered in the first part of his theory ... he produces sufficient proof to show it derived from the Egyptian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For historical/philosophical claims: structure the argument (divide into books/chapters), follow a clear order (geographic or thematic), assemble testimonies and passages from ancient authors, and use comparative evidence to show derivation or consonance. Explicitly state uncertainties where evidence is fragmentary or secret (arcana).

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice of making and preserving exact draughts/engravings of specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the remaining papers is here engraven, and contains the forms of 5 or 6 specimens ... One of the remaining papers is here engraven, and contains the forms of 5 or 6 specimens of different literal characters, cut upon stones at Persepolis ... The figures are taken from certain very clear and transparent stones found in England, of a constant shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record specimens by making exact draughts or engravings and preserve plates/papers. Use consistent figure notation and captions referencing place and collector. Engrave or publish visual records to prevent loss of dispersed papers and to allow comparative study.
